Drawing command bytes reached from $1E76 (pointer in command at $1DDC). The interpreter at $42E1 reads this span while expanding the stream.
Drawing command bytes reached from $1E85 (pointer in command at $1DDC; pointer in command at $1D28). The interpreter at $42E1 reads this span while expanding the stream.
Drawing command bytes reached from $1ECB (pointer in command at $1D1C). The interpreter at $42E1 reads this span while expanding the stream.
Sets flags $05 and emits three-byte cell records for the cluster of tiles $53–$59 up to the $FF return at $1F1D. Both hand-over images contain these commands. No entry is established.
Byte $FF after the retained scenery bytes and before the stream at $1F1F. As a drawing opcode it returns through $43AC.
Drawing stream for actor shape index $06 in the split table read at $4262 and $4267. Calls substream $1F43 before processing its following commands.
Drawing stream for actor shape index $07 in the split table read at $4262 and $4267. Calls substream $BC20 before processing its following commands.

Drawing stream for actor shape index $03 in the split table read at $4262 and $4267. Calls substream $BDEC before processing its following commands.
Drawing stream for actor shape index $04 in the split table read at $4262 and $4267. Calls substream $BE56 before processing its following commands.
Drawing stream for actor shape index $05 in the split table read at $4262 and $4267. Calls substream $BE9C before processing its following commands.
Drawing command bytes reached from $1F43 (pointer in command at $1F1F). The interpreter at $42E1 reads this span while expanding the stream.
Drawing return command $FF, dispatched to $43AC. The alternating page tail begins at the next byte.

79 retained bytes from the unpacked image, between the drawing return at $1FB0 and the bitmap at $2000. Most even addresses contain $74 and most odd addresses $8B. These bytes sit beyond the return command; their original purpose is open.
Operand target of the menu glyph copier at $8362 in the play snapshot. The destination changes with UI row and column.
Calls machine setup at $4BE5 and jumps to game-state initialization at $400F.
Bit mask applied to the combined controls first at $54C0. The interactive symbol handler also tests this mask.
Mask tested at $54C5 to select directional script branch three.
Mask tested at $54CA to select directional script branch two.
Mask used at $54CF for branch one and at $518B by the symbol-control handler.
Mask tested at $54BB to decide whether the cached input must be refreshed.
Mask used by the interactive symbol handler before checking the controls again.
Bit-test operand read by the renderer when deciding how to preserve existing cell attributes.
Clears $46 bytes of game state, sets room 5, the 25-heart counter, the starting spinach and life meter, then runs the menu and initializes the resident room tables and sound.
Operand in the resident startup at $4026. The scene fragment at $C74D tests this address before choosing one of two delivery scene streams.
Operand of the resident load at $4029. The retained code at $C7DB uses it as a countdown decremented before changing a scene.
Operand byte of the resident STY at $4030. The old handler at $C797 reads a cell index here.
Resident instruction at $4033 stores to $0904. The retained handler at $C79A uses its address as a cell-page variable from the older layout.
Resident instruction at $4037 stores to $0934. The retained handler at $C770 uses this address for the target cell.
Operand byte of the resident initialization store at $4037. The retained script at $C768 reads this address as a coordinate in its earlier layout.
Runs a gameplay pass with buffer page $6C, checks the game-state flag, updates the score bonus prescaler, and counts down the love meter every 150 passes.
Clears the input latch, prepares the room buffers, polls controls, runs the intervening $4E79 update and polls again before advancing object scripts.
After the second control poll, transfers to the actor script dispatcher with a tail jump.
Initialized to $FF so the first gameplay pass takes the room rebuild branch. Compared with and updated from $0925.
Rebuilds the static room cache on a room-index change. Clears the foreground mask bit in cached triples and draws depth layers 0 through 2, interleaving input polls.
Uses the room index to choose a four-by-four window in a page group. Draws nonzero scenery entries with bit 7 clear using the split pointers at $1000 and $1038.
For a selected depth layer, draws scenery entries whose high bit is set and draws the eligible item classes from the high nibble of the adjacent map plane. Skips zero and item class seven.
Base used with command bytes $F0–$FF to reach the low vector table at $42FB. The base itself is inside earlier code.
Indexing this base with $F0–$FF reaches the high vector bytes at $430B.
Visits a six-by-six window around the room grid. Every set bit in its fourth plane selects an actor slot. The slot's shape index and cell-relative offsets select a stream and its draw position.
Copies the current cell coordinates into the stream renderer's coordinates before falling through.
Initializes drawing state and walks the stream at $8C/$8D. Values from $F0 up dispatch through the split command table using an indirect jump.
Split pointers indexed by drawing command $F0 through $FF at $42EE and $42F3.
Handles stream bytes below $F0 on the rendering path. The first bounds check tests the row coordinate in $8E against 24.
Clears the temporary drawing mode and restores saved Y before returning. Shared by drawing opcodes $F0, $F1, $F2 and $FF.
Adds the next two bytes to row and column respectively and continues at the next command.
Saves the stream pointer, draws from the little-endian target, restores the caller's stream pointer and skips the pointer bytes.
Takes the next two bytes as the replacement stream pointer and resumes decoding without saving the old stream.
Reads a count into $0926, advances the pointer and patches the repeat command with the restart position.
Decrements the repeat counter. Resumes at the saved position if it remains nonzero, otherwise continues from the current pointer.
Low pointer byte patched by $43FF into the repeat path's LDA.
High pointer byte patched by $4404 and used by $4415 to restore the repeat resume address.
Loads a stream parameter into $0928, which changes how the cell decoder obtains a component of each entry.
Loads the next stream byte into $0927. The cell decoder stores it at offset zero of the destination triple.
Increments the counter byte in the current stream, compares it against two thresholds and either skips the five-byte operand, resets and skips it, or transfers through the embedded pointer.
$4463 or $448F stores the inline count here. The random-value and random-stream handlers decrement it to compare against the last valid index.
Uses a four-bit random value with rejection to index a list after the command, then writes the chosen value into the stream and continues there.
Uses a four-bit random value with rejection to choose one of the little-endian pointers after the command.
Reads an effect number from the drawing stream. Effects 2 and 3 are requested in rooms 0 and 1, while other numbers bypass that room test.

Patches $4335 to jump to $4590, initializes two occupancy arrays, and passes drawing streams and a fixed origin to $42C2. Scans touched rows and columns for shape bounds at $75B8 and following, then restores the CMP opcode at $4335. No runtime caller is established.
Immediate operand patched at $44F8 with the selected shape index. The following code scans occupancy arrays to store minimum row and column offsets and maximum extents.
Surviving bounds-scan instructions add horizontal and vertical extents to the shape tables. The setup at $44E5 clears the same addresses as occupancy arrays before drawing.
Start of the column marks in the bounds measurement utility. The initialization loop at $44E8 clears these addresses over the former bounds code before $4590 fills them.

Handler selected when $44C3 changes the opcode at $4335 to JMP. Marks a row at $455C + X and a column at $4574 + Y, then joins the drawing stream advance at $4327. The resident CMP at $4335 instead reads the first byte here.
Low offsets of the working cell rows. $433B adds the selected row's offset to the column contribution when writing a drawing cell.
Old occupancy scan reads $45A7 indexed by row in the retained instructions at $457D. This address overlaps the live low offset table at $459C.
High offsets of the same working rows, added to the active buffer page before writing a drawing cell.
Old occupancy scan uses this indexed address in the retained code at $4563, while live room drawing uses this span as part of the high offset table.
Supplies the low bytes for drawing opcode $F4's indirect dispatch at $45E7.
Supplies the matching high bytes for $F4 subcommands at $45EC. Entries can target drawing code or the descriptor dispatch in the $5100 page.
Reads a subcommand from the current drawing stream and jumps through the low and high handler bytes relative to $45CB and $45D7.
Tests bit 3 of $0903 and chooses between streams $1141 and $1156 before jumping to the renderer.
Code at $4855 sets outcome one, and $4899 sets outcome two. The occupied-cell branch at $48CE schedules the selected reaction.
When bit 1 of $0935 is set, advances $0922 and selects alternate drawing streams on counts 7, 15 and 23, with a separate update at count 23. The counter rolls over at 60.
The cell drawing path tests this byte before updating a destination cell whose layout byte has bit $80 set.
Stores the previous $0929 value before the scenery rebuild switches working pages.
Incremented by $48E0 to choose the next entry in the page of bytes used by the renderer's clear routine.
Value returned by $48EF every third clear-pattern byte. The rebuild seeds it with zero or $76 in room $0F.
Returns $48DF on every third call, with zeros between, via the counter at $48DE.
Builds static scenery in three passes using RAM with I/O hidden. The layer-one and layer-two passes split interleaved scratch-buffer triples into separate pages for later compositing.
Adds three to the scratch pointer at $B0/$B1 and propagates carry into the high byte.
Walks eligible rectangle bounds from $7544 and related tables, scanning the chosen scenery-cache plane and setting bit 6 on nonzero cells that have not already been marked.
Immediate source of the cache-page bias added at $4A79. The renderer uses the result to patch its planar reads at $4A94 and $4AA1.
Low byte of the cache flag load at $4A94. $4A68 seeds it with the row's offset and $4AB2 uses that same value to index a destination cell.
High byte of the cache flag load at $4A94, patched by $4A7B from the source row.
Low byte of the cache write at $4AA1, patched alongside the flag read.
High byte of the cache write at $4AA1. Receives the page value also used by the flag read.
Low byte of the load at $4AA4. The setup computes the same low offset for the cache's three parallel planes.
High byte of the load at $4AA4, patched after adding three to the first source page.
Low byte of the load at $4AA9, patched by the row setup at $4A71.
High byte of the read at $4AA9. The row setup at $4A88 patches it to the third source plane of the scenery cache.
Immediate operand of $4ABB. $4A8E patches it using the triple-offset table while the cache merge computes the destination page for the interleaved cell.
Column comparison operand of CPY at $4AF2 in the cache merge loop.
Row comparison operand of CPY at $4AFA. The rectangle code at $4A56 stores the bottom bound plus one here before scanning.
Patched operand of LDX at $4B01. The cache merge restores its rectangle index before continuing at $4A44.
Addresses the low portion of the planar cache row and the intermediate row index used by $4A65.
$4A74 selects this byte by row and turns it into cache-page offsets for the three source planes.
Generates the low and high bytes of three times the index in pages $7E and $7F for the interleaved draw buffer.
Clears nine pages beginning at $6C00 with all 256 offsets in each page visited in descending order from zero.
Copies nine pages from physical RAM $D000–$D8FF to $6C00–$74FF.
Zeros twelve pages at $6000–$6BFF. The room placement stream fills these planes later in start-up.
Increments the low nibble of Y within a 16-column row. From column 15 wraps to zero while preserving the row.
Decrements the low nibble of Y within a row. At column zero ORs in $0F to wrap to the last column.
Adds $10 to Y, moving down one row of the 16-column grid.
Subtracts $10 from Y, moving up one row of the 16-column grid.

Stops the preceding sound state, sets CIA interrupt routing, copies eight RAM vector bytes and configures the keyboard directions and timer registers. Enables bitmap mode before clearing and initializing the display.
Old call target used by $C73A and $C73D. The resident build holds the high byte of the CIA2 interrupt-register store at this address.
The retained scene code at $C7A5 calls this address as a cell step. The resident game has the operand of the CIA write at $4BF9 here instead.
Returns from machine initialization. Also the destination at $5B28 in the sound IRQ trampoline.
Clears $2000 through $3FFF and $0400 through $07FF before drawing begins.
Builds the split table for eight times the glyph index at $C800 and $C900, then reverses the eight bits of each index into $CA00.
Low bytes of the color-cell row bases. $8334 reads this half to patch the color destination at $835A.
High bytes of the color-cell row bases, read by the menu glyph renderer at $833A.
Low bytes of the bitmap row bases. The glyph copier adds the column's eight-byte offset before patching the bitmap destination.
High bytes of the bitmap row bases. $832B adds the carry and the high portion of the glyph's column offset.
Updates the four-byte state at $4D9F with shifts, addition and carry propagation. Returns its new low byte in A and restores X.
Immediate operand loaded into X just before the random-state helper returns. This preserves the caller's loop index.
Samples the VIC raster into two bytes at $4DA0/$4DA1 and derives an odd byte for $4DA2 from a third sample.
Low byte of the evolving random-state word returned by $4D86.
Second random-state byte seeded directly from the VIC raster at $4D8F.
Third random-state byte seeded by the same raster-sampling loop.
High component of the random state, seeded with an odd value and folded below $80 by the update.
Companion low byte added to $4D9F during the state advance.
Companion second byte used in $4D4C's addition with carry.
Companion third byte updated alongside $4DA1.
Companion high byte tested for feedback wrap at $4D67.
Stores A as the outer loop count. Decrements the inner counter at $4DB7 until it wraps to zero, then repeats for the outer count.
$4DA7 initializes it and $4DAF decrements it after each complete inner loop.
Decremented by $4DAA until zero. The next outer iteration wraps it from zero through 255.
Five CIA port-A row values for the remappable action keys. The scan pairs these with masks at $4DBD and action bits at $4DC2.
Five active-low column masks for the selected rows. A zero AND result means the corresponding key is down.
Five bits ORed into $0940 for successful matrix tests.

Temporarily sets the processor port to $35 for I/O. Scans five keys, merges active-low joystick direction bits from CIA1 port A, advances sound, restores Y and the banking byte, and returns the latched control mask.

Saves A and the banking value, enables I/O and acknowledges CIA1. If the Timer B status bit is set, preserves X and Y around the indirect handler call before restoring banking and returning from interrupt.
RTI entry at the end of the IRQ handler. The interrupt setup installs an IRQ vector ending in this routine's page.
Jumps indirectly through the RAM vector at $FFF8. The timer IRQ reaches this with a JSR, so its handler can return to $4E65.
Four little-endian addresses copied to physical RAM $FFF8–$FFFF by $4BE5. The first is the initial sound callback, followed by NMI, reset and IRQ.

Walks the active rectangle bounds, derives row and byte addresses from coordinate tables, then examines cell triples in the render buffer. Marks visited triples with bit 6 before taking the bitmap write path.
The cell's first byte replaces the bank immediate operand at $4F47 before the tile row address is computed.
Immediate limit for the X loop at $4F0A. The compositor changes it to select the last column in the dirty rectangle.
End-row limit operand of CPY at $4F15. The row scanner iterates again when Y remains below it.
Operand of the LDX at $4F19 reached after the row scan. The jump at $4F1B returns to the renderer's rectangle loop.
Low operand of the color-only store at $4F2A, patched for the screen row.
High byte of the color-cell store at $4F2A. The color-only path uses the same selected screen row as the full tile path.

Loads the cell ID and draw flags from the interleaved buffer. Uses the tile bitmap base table, writes its screen color byte and copies the eight bitmap rows, reversing the bits on the signed-cell path.
Low operand of the store at $4F41, patched like the color-only destination from the row offset table.
High byte of the color-cell store at $4F41. The row setup patches it as the compositor advances.
Immediate value at $4F47 selects the maximum tile bank for the current draw flags. The following code derives the tile pointer from $99FF and $9A06.
Immediate operand of $4F63. The following BMI selects the row bit-reversal path at $4F95. The straight path copies eight rows to the bitmap.
Low operand of LDX at $4F95, patched along with the ordinary tile source.
High byte of the absolute indexed read at $4F95. $4F5E patches it to the selected tile source for reflection through the bit-reversal table.
Maps the six-bit cell color selector to the VIC bitmap screen byte. Used on both the plain-color and tile-copy paths.

Reads the resident stream at $C000. FF FD selects a room origin, FF FE selects a depth group, FF FC supplies a slot index. Other five-byte records place four plane values at a cell offset. The stream ends at FF FF.
For each set bit in the fourth plane's new cell value, records Y and the plane page in the matching 12-byte actor slot.
Writes Y and the third plane's page number as a two-byte pair at $0909 plus twice A.
Pre-increments the absolute operand of its own LDA, then reads the next byte. The installer initializes the operand to $BFFF so the first read is $C000.
Low operand of the byte reader at $5091. The reader increments it before each world stream read.
High operand of LDA at $5091. Incremented when the low byte of the world pointer wraps.
Sets four zero-page pointers to consecutive pages for depth 0, 1 or 2. Groups begin at $6000, $6400 and $6800.
Maps sixteen room indices to offsets within a 16-by-16 plane. Its four groups start at offsets 0, $40, $80 and $C0.
Scans for a zero slot and writes A there, then redraws the inventory. The pickup path checks capacity before calling it.
Finds the first slot equal to A, shifts following bytes one place toward it through destination slot seven, decrements the inventory count and redraws. Returns early if no slot matches.
Copies 18 bytes from $5151 to $5163 at game start.
Low bytes for ten interleaved drawing stream pointers selected by the symbol index at $5210.
High bytes interleaved with $5110 for the ten symbol pictures. $5213 uses the current symbol value doubled.

Advances the symbol game at $521A before selecting its interactive scenery. Enters the selection routine with the mutable descriptor at $5163. The adjacent entries choose alternative descriptors at three-byte intervals.
Eighteen starting bytes copied to $5163 by $5104. The interactive symbol selector changes the copied records.
First byte of the first three-byte interactive symbol descriptor. $5208 can advance it and $520C uses it as a picture index.
Second field of the first three-byte interactive symbol descriptor. Its address can also be reached through $25/$26 when the selector updates the record.
Third byte of the first mutable symbol descriptor, in the six three-byte records accessed by $5175.
Saves the descriptor pointer from A and Y. Tests scene state and actor occupancy one grid row down, then selects the drawing stream from the descriptor and the surrounding state.
Checks $0903 state bits and the six three-byte symbol records. If the target matches, jumps to $5296. Otherwise, on the reroll path, draws six random values from 5 through 14.
Six target bytes compared with the first byte of each three-byte record at $5163.
Compares the target table with six live symbols at stride three and returns Z set when all match.
Requests sound six times, sets bit 5 of $0903, and sets six item-plane cells in page $65 to heart code $10.
Eight records of twelve bytes. The first word is the script position, and the next pair selects the cell in the actor mask planes.
Second byte of each twelve-byte actor slot. $4255 copies it as the high part of the current frame address.
Page byte from each live actor record. The bounds pass subtracts the room origin before using its row component.
One byte per actor record added to the row base by the drawing pass at $426F.
Last byte in an actor slot, used as an offset in the actor rectangle computation at $5ECD.
Two zero bytes between the end of the eight active actor slots at $532C and the saved depth at $532F. The 96-byte initialization copy to $52CD ends before these bytes.
Remembers the player layer counter before entry to the linked room so the exit can restore it.
Copies 96 initial bytes from $59F9 to $52CD, for eight 12-byte slots.
Walks the slot index table at $535A, dispatching the corresponding actor scripts through $5361. A zero slot index ends the traversal with a tail call.
Saves the scheduler's current index across the actor script call at $534C.
$5363 saves Y here while a slot runs and $53A0 restores the slot offset before copying the result back.
Byte offsets of six secondary actor records in the order fetched by the actor update loop at $5342.
Copies a 12-byte slot to zero page. Advances its two-byte stream pointer and uses the second byte of a command pair to select a handler when the pair's OR equals $3F and is nonzero.

Looks three pages behind the actor's cell pointer for linked tile types 5 and 6. For type 6 saves the room and cell, installs the stored start-side position, and sets room 5. Type 5 looks up the saved room.
Subtracts four pages from the candidate occupancy plane and uses the bit $10 test shared with $5471.
Moves the candidate index down one row, tests bit $10 in the selected plane and chooses or skips the inline branch.
Reads an inline repeat count, advances the command pointer by one and saves the advanced pointer as the restart address.
Decrements the current repeat counter. If it remains nonzero, restores the saved script pointer from $64/$65.
Attempts to remove inventory item $20. If it cannot, sets bit $04 in $0902 and takes the current actor script branch. The successful removal follows the next branch instead.

Takes the latched mask, tests direction bits in priority order and adds a direction selector from one to four to the script pointer. The hold path clears and polls the latch until one of the four direction bits is present.
Takes a nonzero byte below or above $3F as an index into the actor's pointer table, then loads that address. Zero and $3F return without changing the pointer.
Masks the random state to two bits, advances the actor command pointer by that index, and resolves the byte through the actor's own jump table.
Reads and clears $0920. State one follows the current branch, state two selects $7B7C, and other values enter the cell flag test at $556C.
Moves the candidate cell left then enters the solid-cell check shared with rightward movement.

Moves the candidate cell index right and checks flags in that cell or one row up. A flagged cell requests sound $00 or $0D according to bit $20 and takes the current script branch. An empty pair skips that branch.
Skips the candidate when all eight slots are occupied. Otherwise checks the cell two rows above and chooses the current script branch when an item is present.
Steps up twice from the current actor cell and then uses the common item collection routine.

Tests two candidate cells, branches for class-seven items, and rejects normal pickup at eight slots. Otherwise increments the count, requests sound and clears the item in the plane. Heart pickup updates both the held-heart and remaining-heart counters.
Temporarily subtracts two pages from the actor's plane address, reads the item byte at the same cell then restores the page. Returns Z set if the item byte is zero.
Inspects bit 5 in the adjoining plane when the depth byte at $0934 permits the direction, then selects the normal or alternate script continuation.
Uses the other neighboring plane, four pages from the lower-plane address, and shares the bit-5 test at $567D.
Bypasses the check at the lowest depth. Otherwise selects a lower flag plane before entering the common door test.

Checks the actor depth before selecting the adjacent plane. If the cell's flag bit 5 is set and its scenery code is $81 or $82, checks inventory class three against the cell coordinates linked to each key.
Loads mask $02 for the common scenery flag check.
Loads mask $01 before entering the shared flag check.
Moves the candidate cell index one row up before entering the common branch test with mask $04.
Selects flag bit $08 for the actor branch test at $5731. The shared test reads the plane below the current actor occupancy page.
Moves the candidate plane back four pages and enters the bit $10 test at $5764.
Moves the candidate plane forward four pages and enters the same flag test.
Reads the plane immediately below the occupational pointer and selects the current actor branch when flag bit $10 is clear.
Tries the next depth unless the actor is already at depth two, then tests mask $40 through the flags plane.
Selects the preceding flag plane and tests bit $40, branching through the current script entry when it is set.
Steps a row down in the candidate cell, then enters the bit $80 test at $5793.
Reads the plane immediately below the actor cell and chooses the current script branch when bit $80 is set.
Subtracts one from the vertical subcell offset. When it falls below the signed limit, clears the offset and switches to the next world row upward.
Increments the vertical subcell offset until it reaches six, then clears it and advances one world row downward.
Increments the signed horizontal subcell offset, clamping it to the negative wrap value when it reaches the positive bound.

Clears occupancy at the old cell and advances the index. Crossing a four-column room boundary changes the room index. Crossing the end of the full grid row also wraps the column and adjusts the room index by three.
Decrements the signed horizontal subcell offset and clamps it to the positive wrap value when it drops past the negative bound.

Clears the old occupancy bit and moves one cell left. Crosses to the previous room at a local four-column boundary. At the far left it wraps the column and adjusts the room by three before setting the new occupancy.
Decrements the cell column and begins the room-index update when a leftward move crosses a four-column room boundary.
Decrements the current room index when the leftward move crosses a four-column room boundary, then falls through the shared store.
Writes the destination room index in A. The following movement code records the destination cell and sets its actor bit.
Clears the old actor bit and adds 16 to the cell index. When that crosses a four-row room boundary, updates the room index before recording the new cell.
Increments the foreground depth counter, clears the old bit $20, then uses a four-page step to set that bit at the new depth.
Decrements the foreground depth counter and uses the shared flag update at $58BE after subtracting four pages.
Increments the actor depth counter at $0904 and moves its occupancy to the page four higher.
Decrements the actor depth counter at $0904 and moves its occupancy to the page four lower.
Native command $1C decrements the active actor's vertical subcell offset.
Native command $1D increments the active actor's vertical subcell offset.
Adds one to the actor's horizontal subcell offset and folds out-of-range values to $FC.
Toggles off the old actor occupancy, steps right in Y and commits the new coordinates and mask.
Subtracts one from the actor's horizontal subcell offset and folds out-of-range values to three.
Removes the actor mask from the old cell, moves one cell left and restores occupancy at the new position.
Selects the row above after toggling occupancy at the old cell and saves the new position.
XORs the actor's occupancy at the old depth, advances the page by four and uses $597B to register the position.
Clears occupancy by XOR and subtracts four from the occupancy page before committing the move.
XORs the actor mask out of its old cell, steps down a world row and uses $597B to save the position and toggle the mask into the new cell.
Low byte of each interleaved native actor command address read at $53C0 after the command number has been doubled.
High byte corresponding to $598A. The indirect jump at $53DC uses both bytes.
Interleaved pointers for actor-script commands starting at index one. The dispatcher at $53BE doubles the command index before loading the low and high bytes at $598A and $598B.
Zero byte between the last actor command vector at $59F6–$59F7 and the initial actor slot records at $59F9.
Source of eight 12-byte records copied into active slots at $52CD. The eighth record starts with all fields clear.
Selects parameter set Y and writes the envelope and pulse values to a SID voice register group computed from A. Temporarily exposes the I/O area and restores the prior processor-port value.
The operand of SBC at $5A6A is patched with the voice number. The code shifts the voice three times before subtracting it to obtain seven times that number.

Enables the requested voice slots from the low three bits in A, initializes their stream pointers and first events, and installs sound callbacks in the hardware-RAM and KERNAL IRQ paths when the player was idle.
Reads the CIA1 interrupt register and invokes the sound tick on Timer B. Continues through the saved KERNAL interrupt-vector destination.
$5AED saves the low byte of the KERNAL's IRQ vector here before the music player redirects IRQ.
High byte saved alongside $5B23 and restored by the player when music ends.
Calls the sound tick at $5B2B, then jumps through a patched target for the prior RAM handler.
Saved low byte of the timer callback at $FFF8, restored at $5CDD.
High byte of the saved RAM callback address in the jump operand at $5B28.

When active, counts five timer interrupts before updating the three voices. Handles delayed gate changes, reads new events when a voice duration expires, and takes the shutdown path when the stop flag is set.
Sets the completion flag at $5D25 and returns. The order scheduler tests this flag before selecting another pattern.
Copies each voice's saved base control byte directly to its SID control register, removing the gate bit added by the note player.
Writes the three cached control bytes at $5D0B–$5D0D to SID voices one through three.
Loads CIA1 Timer B with low byte $FF and high byte from $5D23, enables its interrupt source and starts it with a forced reload.
